# Kickoff Review — DESTINATION: DEEP SPACE (2019)

**Generated by the BIOCORE kickoff autorun, 2026-08-24, as an end-to-end beta test.**
This is what the pipeline produces on kickoff morning. The game is 2019 DEEP SPACE, used as a stand-in
for BIOCORE because its outcome is already known and the advice can be checked.

| Label | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **[C]** CONFIRMED | Quoted from the manual with a section/page, or computed by a tool in this repo |
| **[COMPUTED]** | Produced by a script here; reproducible from `results/` |
| **[INFERENCE]** | Reasoning chained off confirmed facts |
| **[S]** SPECULATION | Flagged so it never passes as fact |

**Inputs:** `BRIEFING_PACK.md` · `game_def.json` · `candidates.yaml` · `bom_config.yaml`
**Outputs read:** `results/cycle_model.txt` · `cycle_sweep.txt` · `strategy_ranking.txt` · `bom.txt`

> ⚠ **Era note [C].** This manual predates the 2023 colour convention, so the EVERGREEN/GAMESPEC
> split is unavailable and every rule reads UNKNOWN. The new-this-season set here comes from the
> **rule-id diff against 2018 POWER UP**, not from headline colour. On a real BIOCORE run the colour
> split will be available and is the faster path.

## 1. Game summary [C]

| | |
|---|---|
| Match length | 150 s |
| SANDSTORM PERIOD | **15 s** at the start (manual §5.2 p41) |
| TELEOP | 135 s (derived) |
| Endgame | **No separately-defined phase.** HAB climbs conventionally occur in the closing ~30 s |

**Scoring — manual Table 5-1, p42 [C]**

| Action | Value |
|---|--:|
| SANDSTORM Bonus 1 — BUMPERS fully cross the HAB LINE, started Level 1 | 3 |
| SANDSTORM Bonus 2 — same, started Level 2 | 6 |
| HATCH PANEL — attached to a ROCKET or CARGO SHIP, fully supported, via hook/loop | 2 |
| CARGO — in a BAY with a Null or scored HATCH PANEL, not touching an allied ROBOT | 3 |
| HAB Climb Level 1 / 2 / 3 | 3 / 6 / **12** |

**Ranking Points [C]**
- **HAB Docking** — alliance earns ≥ **15** HAB Climb Bonus points → 1 RP
- **Complete ROCKET** — ≥1 ROCKET with **6 HATCH PANELS and 6 CARGO** → 1 RP
- Win 2 RP / Tie 1 RP

**Field geometry that constrains every design [C]** — manual §4.10 vision targets, p35:
- Lowest **ROCKET PORT** top: 3 ft 3⅛ in ≈ **39 in**
- Lowest **ROCKET HATCH** top: 2 ft 7½ in ≈ **31.5 in** (same as CARGO SHIP and LOADING STATION hatches)

> **DEEP SPACE has no low goal.** Every scoring location is ≥ 31 in off the carpet. This single fact
> drives §4 and is the kind of number `03_ARCHETYPE_CORPUS.md` §2.4 means by *"find this number first."*

## 2. Scoring strategy [COMPUTED]

From `results/cycle_model.txt` at a **12 s cycle, 2 AUTO units** — both robot-design assumptions, not
manual facts, and both echoed with their source in the tool's CONSTANTS table.

| Endgame choice | cycles | TOTAL pts |
|---|--:|--:|
| none | 11.2 | 39.8 |
| HAB Climb L1 | 10.8 | 41.5 |
| HAB Climb L2 | 10.2 | 42.8 |
| **HAB Climb L3** | 9.2 | **45.5** |

**Break-even — is the climb worth the cycles it costs?**

| Action | pts | time | cycles lost | pts lost | NET |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| HAB L1 | 3 | 5 s | 0.42 | 1.2 | **+1.8** |
| HAB L2 | 6 | 12 s | 1.00 | 3.0 | **+3.0** |
| HAB L3 | 12 | 25 s | 2.08 | 6.2 | **+5.8** |

All three pay. **[INFERENCE]** But the margin is small in absolute terms — L3 nets under 6 points, about
two cycles — so a climb that fails, or that costs more than 25 s, is immediately negative. This is the
opposite of the 2026 case, where the endgame was 1.1 % of scoring; here it is ~13–26 % of a robot's own output.

**Ranking-point feasibility [COMPUTED]**

| RP | threshold | you alone | alliance ×3 | reachable |
|---|--:|--:|--:|---|
| HAB Docking | 15 climb pts | n/a | n/a | fixed-action based — see break-even |
| Complete ROCKET | 12 units | 13 | 40 | **YES solo** — *but see the caveat* |

> **The model overstates Complete ROCKET.** It treats the threshold as 12 cycle units. The real
> requirement is 6 HATCH **and** 6 CARGO **on one rocket** — a co-ordination and sequencing problem,
> not a volume one, and CARGO does not count until a HATCH is present in that BAY. `game_def.json`
> records this limitation inline. **Do not plan around "YES solo."** [C]

**Assumptions declared, per the CONSTANTS table:** `per_cycle = 1` (a DEEP SPACE round trip delivered
one game piece — ASSUMPTION); all `time_s` climb durations are estimates. Every point value and RP
threshold is sourced to Table 5-1.

## 3. Ranked strategies [COMPUTED]

From `results/strategy_ranking.txt`. **The quadrant is the decision; the tier is a delivery-risk badge.**

| # | id | Strategy | ACH | VAL | Quadrant | Tier | Binding constraint |
|--:|---|---|--:|--:|---|---|---|
| 1 | D8 | Minimal-and-flawless (hatch only) | 100.0 | 68.6 | **BUILD THIS** | T1 GREEN | A1 build-hours fit 5/5 |
| 2 | D6 | Defender / denial | 98.4 | 67.6 | **BUILD THIS** | T1 GREEN | A7 programming 4/5 |
| 3 | D7 | HATCH PANEL feeder / support | 100.0 | 56.6 | **BUILD THIS** | T1 GREEN | A1 build-hours fit 5/5 |
| 4 | D1 | Cargo ship bulk scorer | 81.5 | 77.9 | **BUILD THIS** | T1 GREEN | A4 drive-practice sensitivity |
| 5 | D2 | Rocket level-1 specialist | 63.5 | 86.9 | BUILD THIS | **T4 GATED** | G2 WORKSTREAMS: 2 new streams |
| 6 | D5 | SANDSTORM / auto specialist | 75.6 | 59.0 | **BUILD THIS** | T1 GREEN | A5 reliability 3/5 |
| 7 | D3 | Full-rocket robot (levels 1–3) | 33.9 | 95.2 | TRAP | T4 GATED | G2: 3 novel mechanisms |
| 8 | D9 | Do-everything | 22.0 | 97.6 | TRAP | T4 GATED | G1 MACHINE: needs CNC |
| 9 | D4 | HAB Level 3 climb specialist | 45.2 | 63.4 | TRAP | T4 GATED | G2 WORKSTREAMS |

**Reading this for a 15-student team**

- **D1 Cargo ship bulk scorer is the recommendation.** It is the only row combining a top-quartile
  value (77.9) with an ungated T1 GREEN. D8/D6/D7 rank higher on the index purely on achievability —
  they are safe, but D8 and D7 cap your ceiling and D6 scores nothing itself.
- **D3 and D9 are the trap pair**, and they carry the *highest* value scores (95.2, 97.6). That is the
  whole point of the two-axis model: the most attractive strategies on value are the ones that gate.
- **D4 (HAB L3) gates** despite the climb having the best break-even in §2. Break-even asks "is it
  worth the cycles"; the gate asks "can you build it at all." Both are true. [INFERENCE]
- **D2 is the near miss** — highest ungated value at 86.9, blocked only by needing a second workstream.
  If anything frees capacity, D2 is the upgrade path from D1.

## 4. Recommended design + BOM [COMPUTED]

**Design:** KOP chassis + under-bumper intake + **telescoping arm** + bumpers + baseline electrical.

| Gate | Value | Limit |
|---|---|---|
| BUDGET | **$2,494.49** discretionary (gross $4,725.49 − $2,231.00 KOP credit) | $2,500.00 |
| TOOLING FLOOR | bandsaw_drillpress | bandsaw_drillpress |
| BUILD / DESIGN / PROGRAMMING HOURS | 99.0 / 38.0 / 66.0 h | 129.8 / 74.9 / 134.8 |
| PARALLEL WORKSTREAMS | 3 effective (5 mechanisms) | 3 |
| NOVEL MECHANISMS | 2 | 2 |
| MOTOR COUNT | 6 motors / 6 controllers | 12 |
| **GEOMETRY (REACH)** | telescoping_arm reaches **78 in** | **39 in** |

**How it reaches the scoring aperture:** the telescoping arm lifts the manipulator to the 39 in ROCKET
level-1 PORT, with 39 in of headroom.

**EARLIEST ORDER-BY: 2026-11-21** — the baseline electrical package is 6-week lead, high stockout.

### The design converged through three gate failures — this is the useful part [COMPUTED]

| Attempt | Gate that failed | Why | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **GEOMETRY** | over-bumper intake reaches 12 in; every DEEP SPACE target is ≥31 in | add a lift |
| 2 | **TOOLING FLOOR** | virtual four-bar needs `mill_lathe`; team has `bandsaw_drillpress` | telescoping arm instead |
| 3 | **BUDGET** | $2,570.28 vs $2,500 | under-bumper intake (−$76) |

Attempt 1 is exactly the failure the rehearsal grade called fatal — a fully costed, scheduled robot
with no legal path to the goal. The gate caught it in seconds. Final margin is **$5.51**.

## 6. Loopholes and edge cases

Run on **both mandatory axes** per `CLAUDE.md`.

### 6a. Strategic ambiguity

**Undefined ALL-CAPS used in the body but never defined [COMPUTED]** — `UNDEFINED_CAPS.tsv`:

| Token | count | Read |
|---|--:|---|
| DESTINATION / DEEP / SPACE | 27 each | game-title fragments — noise, correctly ignorable |
| **WITHOLDING** | 3 | **misspelling of WITHHOLDING ALLOWANCE** — a defined term rendered unsearchable [C] |
| DISQUALIFICATION | 3 | used as a defined consequence but not glossed |
| **CLIMB** | 2 | appears as "Cumulative HAB CLIMB points" in the ranking rules while the glossary defines HAB Climb Bonus — a scoring term with two spellings |
| BLDC / WAGO / DMC / UTC / ABC | 2–5 | vendor and unit acronyms — noise |

The genuinely load-bearing hits are **WITHOLDING** and **CLIMB**: both are scoring- or
eligibility-relevant terms whose spelling differs from the glossary entry. [INFERENCE]

**Rule-level edge cases from the manual text [C]**
- **CARGO requires a HATCH first.** CARGO counts only "in a BAY with a Null HATCH PANEL or scored
  HATCH PANEL." A CARGO-only robot scores nothing unless a partner or a Null panel precedes it.
- **"Not in contact with a ROBOT from that ROCKET/CARGO SHIP'S ALLIANCE."** Your own robot touching
  the CARGO voids it; an **opponent** touching it does not. Asymmetric, and easy to misread.
- **HATCH PANEL support is explicitly opponent-proof:** "contact by an opponent ROBOT does not count
  as 'support' and does not negate a scored HATCH PANEL."
- **HAB climb eligibility:** a ROBOT "whose BUMPERS haven't fully crossed their HAB LINE to leave
  their HAB ZONE at any point during the MATCH isn't eligible" — a robot that never leaves scores
  **zero** climb points regardless of where it ends.
- **One per HATCH / one per BAY** caps both scoring actions.

### 6b. Inspection / construction ambiguity — the axis the rehearsal missed

`reference/QA-AMBIGUITY-HOTSPOTS.md` establishes bumpers as the #1 real-confusion cluster across
2024–2026 (116 questions across the bumper six). 2019's analogues, from the extracted rules:

| Rule | Subject [C] |
|---|---|
| **R30** | BUMPERS "must weigh no more than 15 lbs" |
| **R31** | backing "¾ in. (nominal) thick by 5 in. ± ½ in. tall" |
| **R33** | support: "a minimum of ½ in. at each end of each BUMPER wood segment" |
| R25 | the 7½ in. virtual horizontal plane defining the BUMPER ZONE |
| R27 | "installation and removal to facilitate inspection and weighing" |

These carry explicit tolerances (`± ½ in.`, `minimum ½ in.`) — tolerance language is where inspection
disputes concentrate. **Read the R25–R33 block before any CAD**, because bumper geometry constrains
the frame perimeter. [INFERENCE]

### 6c. Penalty arbitrage — is breaking the rule worth more than obeying it?

- **Touching your own scored CARGO** voids 3 points and costs nothing else. There is no scenario where
  deliberately voiding your own score pays. Not exploitable.
- **Opponent contact cannot negate a scored HATCH PANEL** — so defensive contact aimed at *unscoring*
  is worthless. Defense in DEEP SPACE must deny *access*, not undo *scores*. That is a real strategic
  conclusion, and it is why D6 scores 5/5 on denial value. [INFERENCE]
- **HAB LINE eligibility** is binary and free to satisfy: crossing costs ~3 s and unlocks up to 12
  climb points. Never skip it.

## 7. Pitfalls for this team

1. **Building for the rocket without measuring 39 in first.** The pipeline caught this; a student
   would not. Every DEEP SPACE target is ≥31 in and there is no low goal.
2. **Chasing Complete ROCKET.** The model says "YES solo" and the model is wrong — it is a
   co-ordination requirement, not a volume one.
3. **Chasing HAB Docking.** 15 alliance points is not three L1 climbs (9). It needs L3+L2 or L2×2+L1.
4. **Believing the highest-value strategies.** D3 and D9 top the value axis and both gate.
5. **The $5.51 budget margin.** One price change breaks it. Re-run before the 2026-11-21 order date.
6. **A CARGO-first robot.** Without a HATCH in the BAY it scores zero.

## 8. Q&A questions to file in week 1

Ranked by leverage. **Both axes represented**, as required.

| # | Axis | Rule | Question |
|--:|---|---|---|
| 1 | inspection | **R31 / R33** | Does the "± ½ in." backing-height tolerance apply to the wood alone or to the assembled BUMPER including fabric? |
| 2 | inspection | **R30** | Is the 15 lb BUMPER limit per-set or per-side? |
| 3 | strategic | **Table 5-1 / CARGO** | If an allied ROBOT contacts a scored CARGO *momentarily*, is the point voided for that scoring cycle only, or re-evaluated continuously? |
| 4 | strategic | **HATCH PANEL** | Does "fully supported ... via the hook/loop tape" require the tape to bear load, or only to be in contact? |
| 5 | strategic | **HAB Climb** | Must the HAB LINE crossing be completed before the climb, or at any point in the MATCH? |
| 6 | inspection | **R25** | Is the 7½ in. BUMPER ZONE plane measured with the ROBOT on carpet or on the HAB PLATFORM? |

Questions 1, 2 and 6 attach to the inspection cluster, which historically carries ~20 % of a season's
Q&A volume and is the cluster that stops a robot playing at all.

## Scouting: name the endgame structure

**The endgame structure is the HAB PLATFORM.** Per `reference/SCOUTING-PLAN.md`, FMS publishes
`Avg <endgame>` every season (4/4 seasons), so the free-data column would be **`Avg HAB Climb`** —
alongside `Ranking Score`, `Avg Match`, `Avg Auto`, `Record`, `DQ`, `Played`, `Total RP`.

Scout only the 22 gap fields: breakdowns and cause, defense quality, endgame **attempted** vs
succeeded, driver skill, and `known_weaknesses`.

## Known limitations
- **`per_cycle = 1` and all climb `time_s` values are assumptions**, and every §2 number inherits them.
- The cycle model handles **one** repeatable action; DEEP SPACE has two (CARGO 3, HATCH 2). The HATCH
  half is not modelled here and would need a second run.
- **Achievability was scored by the same agent writing this review.** The rubric assumes two
  independent scorers who reconcile. Treat individual factor scores as `[SPECULATION]`; the quadrants
  and the gates are the trustworthy outputs.
- Rule *headlines* for some 2019 rules captured a body line rather than the true headline — the
  pre-2024 gutter layout puts the headline on a following line and the one-line lookahead is
  imperfect. Rule **IDs and counts are exact** (169, matching `rule-inventory.py`).
